topic: SE Lab Week 3: Git Workflows and Merge Conflicts

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements correctly defines code collaboration as taught?
options: Code collaboration refers to the process of multiple people working together on the same codebase.
Code collaboration is the practice of a single developer merging multiple unrelated projects into one repository.
Code collaboration involves using automated tools to replace human developers entirely.
Code collaboration means assigning different tasks to team members without sharing any code.
questions.correctAnswer: Code collaboration refers to the process of multiple people working together on the same codebase.
questions.explanation: The taught definition states that code collaboration is the process of multiple people working together on the same codebase.

questions.questionText: What is a likely consequence of ignoring merge conflicts when collaborating with Git?
options: Git will automatically delete the conflicting files from the repository
The merged code may contain errors that cause the application to malfunction
The repository will become read‑only for all collaborators
All future pull requests will be rejected by the remote server
questions.correctAnswer: The merged code may contain errors that cause the application to malfunction
questions.explanation: When conflicts are ignored, Git merges the differing versions without resolution, leaving contradictory code in the file. This can introduce bugs or runtime errors, affecting the functionality of the application. The evidence describes conflicts as a normal part of team development that must be resolved to avoid such problems.

questions.questionText: Which command correctly creates a patch file for the commit with hash abc1234 using the -1 flag?
questions.explanation: The -1 flag tells git format-patch to create a patch for exactly one commit. The syntax is: git format-patch -1 <commit-hash>. This generates a .patch file such as 0001-Your-commit-message.patch.
